segments.text: Today we look at enzymes, and why a small change in temperature can stop one working.
Take amylase, the enzyme in your saliva that starts breaking starch down into sugar.
Does that mean amylase stops working if the mouth is very cold?
It slows down a lot. Cold does not break the enzyme, but heat above about 45 degrees can.
For next week, read chapter 4 and write down three questions about the lock and key model.

summary.title: In short
summary.text: Enzymes speed up reactions in the body. Temperature changes how well they work, and strong heat can damage them for good.
